title: Haemolysis in blood samples drawn through peripheral intravenous catheters versus venepuncture: a systematic review and meta-analysis with technique subgroups
abstract: Objective: to estimate the association between catheter draws and haemolysis and to examine whether technique, catheter gauge, collector training and transport explain conflicting results. Design: registered systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis. Results and conclusions will be written after the analysis.
introduction: Published estimates of haemolysis with catheter draws range from several-fold to almost no difference. Emergency departments value catheter draws because they avoid extra needle sticks, while laboratories see rejected samples.
methods: Librarian-designed search, dual screening and extraction, RoB 2 and ROBINS-I, GRADE certainty, random-effects meta-analysis separately for randomised and non-randomised studies, four pre-specified effect modifiers and prediction intervals.
results: Not yet written. The section will report study flow, study characteristics, pooled estimates with prediction intervals by design group, subgroup analyses and GRADE certainty.
discussion: The discussion will state whether technique explains the conflict and what that means for an emergency collection policy that weighs haemolysis against extra needle sticks.
limitations: Mostly non-randomised primary studies with heterogeneous definitions; limited paediatric data.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will be worded by GRADE certainty.
summary: PRISMA-structured draft with results left empty until analysis.
